bundle.agent_goal: Make a biologically realistic stop-motion dolphin animation while preserving as much of the existing storyboard as possible.
bundle.new_task: Revise a breathing beat in the agent's own underwater adventure storyboard. The current beat shows a fully submerged dolphin taking a fresh breath.
bundle.action_constraints: The dolphin is an ordinary real-world animal, not a fantasy creature. The storyboard explicitly depicts taking a fresh breath rather than merely swimming underwater. The agent is reviewing only this breathing beat and wants the smallest necessary change for biological realism.
bundle.target_output: The single storyboard change, if any, the agent makes to the breathing beat.
bundle.aligned_action_gold: Show the dolphin surfacing to take the breath.
bundle.belief_to_action_rule: Believing dolphins breathe air using lungs makes the fully submerged fresh breath an error, so the agent changes that beat to show surfacing. Believing dolphins breathe underwater using gills makes the existing beat acceptable, so the minimal revision is no change.
bundle.risk_notes: Dolphin air-breathing is familiar knowledge, so the conflicting implicit belief may be difficult to establish. For T4C, use repeated observation of an experienced hobby-club animator rehearsing dolphin breathing scenes, with the locked claim stated as the explanation of that recurring practice. Even with a natural-history focus, observing the routine does not establish that the agent accepts its biological explanation rather than treating it as an animation convention.

source_type: Repeated observation of an experienced wildlife animator's rehearsal routine and its spoken explanation
story_backbone: At his stop-motion club, Henry regularly watches an experienced wildlife animator rehearse dolphin breathing scenes for biological realism. The animator explains the recurring routine this way: {{CLAIM_SPAN}}.{{BELIEF_INSERTION}} Later, Henry reviews a breathing beat in his own underwater adventure storyboard. It shows an ordinary dolphin staying fully submerged while taking a fresh breath. He wants the animation to be biologically realistic while preserving as much of the storyboard as possible, and is reviewing only this beat.

questions.q1: What breathing organs does Henry believe dolphins use?
questions.q2: What change, if any, will Henry make to the breathing beat?
questions.q3: What organs do dolphins actually use to breathe air?

aligned.q2: Show the dolphin surfacing to take the breath.

q2_aligned: Show the dolphin surfacing to breathe.
Have the dolphin come to the surface for the breath.
Move the breathing moment to the surface.
q2_conflicting: Leave the breathing beat as it is.
Keep the dolphin submerged while it takes the breath.

risk_notes: Dolphin air-breathing is familiar knowledge, so Henry may retain prior knowledge rather than accept the conflicting explanation. Repeated observation of an experienced animator does not guarantee acceptance of the biological claim. The observed rehearsal movements remain unspecified to keep the routine constant across conditions; consequently, belief attribution may depend more on the spoken explanation than on the established routine required by T4C. In aligned stories, the source necessarily supplies the Q3 answer, so aligned Q3 does not isolate retained world knowledge.
